newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo says Brazzaville shell was a provocation.
newsitem.headline: New Congo says Brazzaville shell was a provocation.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo said on Tuesday a shell which landed in Kinshasa from fighting in Congo's capital Brazzaville on Monday was a deliberate act of provocation.
"We consider this act as a provocation and an aggression by a foreign country," Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha told a news conference in Kinshasa.
"We warn the two warring parties of the conflict in Congo that any repetition will be considered as an attack on the security and sovereignty of the Democratic Republic of the Congo."
Fighting in Brazzaville went into a sixth day on Tuesday as soldiers and militiamen loyal to President Pascal Lissouba battled a political militia loyal to ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso.
The shell which landed in Kinshasa on Monday caused minimal damage when it fell in the garden of a Nigerian diplomat.
"Given the range and 125 mmm calibre of the cannon that experts say was used to fire the shell we have concluded that it was a deliberate act," Karaha said.

However a senior western military source in Kinshasa said he was surprised more shells had not landed in Kinshasa from Brazzaville, given that it is less than three km (two miles) away across the Congo river.
"Shells are going all over the place in Brazzaville," he said.
Laurent Kabila's forces last month drove former president Mobutu Sese Seko from the capital of the former Zaire and renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
